predecessors.name: Italian Republic
predecessors.text: the province of Trieste and north-western Istria, Italian before 1945 and under Allied and Yugoslav military administration from June 1945 along the Morgan Line

successors.name: Italian Republic
successors.text: Zone A and Trieste, handed to Italy: Allied troops left by 24 October 1954, Italian troops entered on 25 October, General De Renzi took control on 26 October

successors.name: Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia
successors.text: Zone B, 'annexed by Yugoslavia, along with nine villages previously in Zone A' under the London Memorandum of 5 October 1954

ledger.x: 15 September 1947: the Free Territory of Trieste comes into existence.
15 September 1947: Zone A is administered by the Allied Military Government.
15 September 1947: British forces in Zone A (same sentence).
15 September 1947: Zone B is administered by the Yugoslav army.
25 October 1954: Italian troops take over Trieste from the Allies.
25 October 1954: British forces leave Zone A (same sentence).
26 October 1954: Zone A goes to Italy.
October 1954: Zone B and nine villages go to Yugoslavia.
October 1954: the Yugoslav army's administration of Zone B ends in annexation; the page gives no day for the Yugoslav side.
5 October 1954: the London Memorandum ends the Free Territory.

certainty.note: The outer border was fixed by the 1947 peace treaty and the line between the zones followed the Morgan Line of 1945; the pages give no coordinates, so Zone B is approximated by municipalities and a circle.
